thread:
oncall-bot: Paging page oncall: prefix-cache errors spiking for /v1/generate routes (error rate -> 6.2% over 5m). Possible KV eviction anomaly. Please acknowledge.
oncall-bot: Incident severity: S2. Affected customers: subset of enterprise tenants in us-west1.
alice_ng: acked. I'm oncall and looking. Can someone grab current top errors and make a quick blast assessment?
carla_sre: I'm pulling metrics now. Latency is fine but we see increased `model_response_mismatch` traces and 500s flagged from runtime indicating cache lookup returned stale pointers -> eviction race suspected.
carla_sre: toplog tail: ```ERROR runtime/cache.go:412 kvcache: eviction failed for key prefix=tenant:acme:conv:abc123 reason=concurrency_eviction_mismatch```
carla_sre: Also seeing a surge in cache bypasses for small prefixes which correlate with customer mismatch reports.
dmitri_eng: tagging in — we deployed a kernel-level eviction fix yesterday on dedicated pools. Might be a regression in the eviction confirmation path when batching is high. Investigating commit 4f9b2a3.
alice_ng: Ok immediate mitigation: we should avoid correctness impact for customers. Proposal: temporarily bypass prefix/KV cache for the affected tenant cohort and apply a short rate-cap on those routes to reduce pressure. Anyone object?
pm_jordan: +1 to bypass for safety. Need to notify support and affected customers if we flip cache behavior.
support_leah: I'll draft a message once we confirm scope. Can you include list of tenant IDs?
carla_sre: Tenant list from traces: tenant:acme, tenant:zephyr, tenant:ora-enterprise. I'll send IDs to you in DM.
dmitri_eng: For bypass we can flip `prefix_cache.enabled=false` for those tenant tags in the routing layer. I have a CLI snippet ready: ```redwoodctl tenant-config set --tenant=tenant:acme --key=prefix_cache.enabled --value=false --env=prod --region=us-west1``` will take effect in ~30s.```
ops-bot: Deploy job queued: config-update/tenant-prefix-bypass (owner=dmitri_eng). CI checks passed.
alice_ng: Let's also apply a soft rate cap to the affected tenants to avoid thrashing while bypass is active: reduce `burst` to 10r/s and `sustained` to 5r/s for those tenants. dmitri, can you apply?
dmitri_eng: Applying now. CLI: ```redwoodctl ratecap update --tenant=tenant:acme --burst=10 --sustained=5 --region=us-west1``` Repeat for zephyr + ora-enterprise.
ops-bot: Ratecap update succeeded for tenant:acme. Changes propagated to edge in ~12s.
carla_sre: After bypass + ratecap: error rate dropped to 0.4% within 2m. Request latency unchanged. No further mismatches in sampled traces.
alice_ng: Good. Support@, please start notifying customers with a short incident note: what happened, immediate mitigation (cache bypass + throttling), and we are doing root cause. Limit to tenants list.
support_leah: Draft: "We observed inconsistent responses for some requests due to a cache eviction race. We've temporarily disabled prefix caching for your tenant and applied a short rate limit to stabilize traffic. This may increase per-request cost/latency slightly. We'll follow up with RCA and ETA for permanent fix." Sending to affected customers now.
pm_jordan: Add SLA impact note? Any breaches?
carla_sre: No SLA breaches yet. We recorded elevated error counts but still under 99.9% for the window. Marking possible degradation; will update if it crosses thresholds.
dmitri_eng: Quick root cause note: under heavy batching the eviction confirmation callback could be processed out-of-order due to a goroutine scheduling bug, leading to a stale entry being served briefly. I have a local patch that sequences confirmations; running local stress.
alice_ng: Plan: keep bypass + ratecap for 2 hours while patch is validated. If validated, we'll schedule a canary deploy to one Dedicated pool, monitor for 30m, then roll forward. Who owns the deployment?
dmitri_eng: I'll own canary deploy. Carla will monitor.
ops-bot: canary-deploy triggered by dmitri_eng: image=eviction-fix:v1-canary target=dedicated-pool-3 region=us-west1
carla_sre: Monitoring dashboards: `prefix_mismatch`, `cache_eviction_failures`, `errors_5xx` on watch. If `prefix_mismatch` >0.5% (30s) revert.
alice_ng: Oncall handoff: I'll keep primary until 20:00 UTC, then @carla_sre takes over for post-mortem and customer follow-ups. Alerting oncall escalation paused for this thread.
support_leah: Customers notified. One customer replied asking for ETA and whether data could be affected — I've told them no data loss, just temporary correctness inconsistency, and we'll follow up with RCA.
dmitri_eng: Canary looks good after 18m: no mismatch traces, eviction failures down to baseline. Preparing roll.
ops-bot: rollout job started: eviction-fix rollout -> dedicated pools us-west1/us-east1 (batch=2) (initiator=dmitri_eng).
carla_sre: After first batch (dedicated-pool-3) we saw stable metrics for 40m. Proceeding to second batch.
ops-bot: rollout batch 2 completed.
alice_ng: Great. Re-enable prefix cache for tenants once rollout is fully healthy and remove temporary ratecaps. dmitri, can you re-enable and remove rate caps? Make sure we do it per-tenant to avoid surprises.
dmitri_eng: Re-enabling prefix cache for tenant:acme now. CLI: ```redwoodctl tenant-config set --tenant=tenant:acme --key=prefix_cache.enabled --value=true --env=prod --region=us-west1``` then remove ratecap: ```redwoodctl ratecap delete --tenant=tenant:acme --region=us-west1```
ops-bot: prefix cache re-enabled for tenant:acme. Ratecap deleted.
carla_sre: Post-change telemetry looks normal. Error rate stable at baseline. No customer complaints in last 25m.
alice_ng: Incident summary for notes: - Impact: correctness mismatches for small prefix lookups for 3 enterprise tenants (brief window) - Mitigations: tenant-level prefix cache bypass + temporary rate caps -> canary + rollout of eviction-fix -> re-enable cache and remove caps - Owners: mitigation (alice_ng, carla_sre), fix/deploy (dmitri_eng) - Customer comms: support_leah sent notices.
pm_jordan: Please add to incident tracker with severity S2 and estimated MTTR 1.5h. I'll create the ticket.
support_leah: I'll follow up with customers with RCA once PM/Eng write it up.
dmitri_eng: Follow-ups: I'll open PR with test harness to reproduce eviction race under high concurrent batching and add integration test to prevent regression.
carla_sre: Assigning follow-up action: postmortem owner = carla_sre, deadline EOD tomorrow.
alice_ng: Thanks everyone. Handing off monitoring to @carla_sre for next shift. I'll update pager duty. :white_check_mark:
